title: 2004 AMC 10B Problem 9
statement: A square has sides of length \(10,\) and a circle centered at one of its vertices has radius \(10.\) What is the area of the union of the regions enclosed by the square and the circle?

solutions.text:
The square has area \(10^2 = 100\) and the circle has area \(\pi(10)^2 = 100\pi.\)

Since the circle is centered at a vertex of the square, exactly one quarter of the circle, area \(25\pi,\) lies inside the square.

The union has area \(100 + 100\pi - 25\pi = 100 + 75\pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Add the areas of the square and the circle, then subtract the overlap
The overlap is the quarter of the circle that lies inside the square
